newsitem.title: GERMANY: Italy's Prodi to visit Kohl for Euro talks in Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi to visit Kohl for Euro talks in Bonn.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi visits Bonn on Thursday evening for talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl which will probably focus on the European Union, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
Prodi was due to meet Kohl for private talks over dinner at Kohl's private bungalow in the grounds of the chancellery shortly after a photo call at 1715 GMT.

The spokesman said he did not know how long the talks would last, but Prodi was expected to return to Rome later in the evening. The talks would end late and there were no plans to hold a news conference afterwards, he said.
Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar visited Germany on Tuesday for private talks with the German leader over dinner.

EU officials say Italy and Spain have relatively slim chances of meeting all the Maastricht Treaty requirements for economic and monetary union (EMU) despite their recent efforts to tighten fiscal controls in order to qualify.

The two meetings within the space of a week have fuelled speculation Kohl might start to discuss a compromise allowing Spain and Italy to join the commmon European currency after it is launched in 1999 -- an idea favoured by some EU officials.
The Spanish government said after Aznar's meeting with Kohl that the German leader had backed Spain's measures to whip its finances into shape for a single European currency.
But it did not say whether Kohl had broached the thorny subject of which countries would be launching the single currency, the Euro, in 1999.
